subject: Clarify archival sunset vs. tenant-scoped erasure — Medicorp evidence and CAIQ mapping
messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena.morris@medicorp.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: LegalOps <legalops@medicorp.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data lifecycle clarifications and CAIQ mapping request

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call last week. As we prepare Medicorp's SIG/CAIQ review and our legal team's SOC 2 evidence pull, we have two closely-related asks that surfaced and I want to make sure we're aligned before we proceed: 

1) "Archival sunset" vs "tenant-scoped erasure" — we need a written definition for both as you use them. Specifically: when data is moved to archival storage, is it considered "retained" for SAR/FOIA/other requests, or is it functionally offline/unrecoverable for normal product flows?

2) Evidence package — Medicorp requires artifact-level proof that tenant-scoped erasure is irreversible when executed (we're comfortable with a staged archival period, but need to confirm what triggers the final purge and that artifacts/logs proving purge are created). Please map the relevant CAIQ/SIG questions (or SOC 2 control refs) to Redwood artifacts you can produce.

I've attached a short intake doc that lists our desired artifacts and time windows (medicorp_retention_request_v1.docx). Can you confirm what you can provide, approximate delivery timeline, and whether we'll need an exception/agreement for any deviations?

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a 30 min call if that's easier.

Best,
Elena
Head of Data Security
Medicorp

Attachment: medicorp_retention_request_v1.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@medicorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data lifecycle clarifications and CAIQ mapping request

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the intake doc. Quick summary of what Redwood will provide and our proposed next steps: 

Summary answers (high level):
- "Archival sunset": our term for the configured retention boundary after which archived blobs are permanently deleted by the storage lifecycle job. During the archival period data is stored in encrypted buckets and is retrievable via controlled internal tooling for operational/debug needs (subject to access logs and approvals).
- "Tenant-scoped erasure": an explicit, customer-initiated deletion (API/Support flow) that removes live copies and dependent caches and then triggers background sweeps to remove archived copies. When complete, the operation is irreversible from an operational standpoint; we generate delete-confirm artifacts and retention audit logs.

What we can deliver to Medicorp within 7 business days: 
- CAIQ/SIG mapping spreadsheet with links to our SOC 2 controls and the specific artifacts (exports, audit logs, retention lifecycle config) you requested.
- An "archival sunset playbook" PDF that shows lifecycle policies, purge triggers, and the retention-job runbook (redwood_archival-sunset-playbook.pdf).
- A sample proof-of-delete package for a synthetic tenant (tombstone + purge job logs + storage object delete entries). We can redact the synthetic IDs but include the exact command/output you could expect.

Open items we want to confirm with you: 
1) Desired retention granularity (tenant-level vs. tenant+dataset level) — intake doc suggests tenant-level 90/365 windows; confirm if Medicorp needs dataset-specific windows.
2) If you require notarized or certified destruction letters (legal sign-off), we may need your procurement/legal to sign an exception/acknowledgement before executing the sample purge on real tenant data.

Next steps: Priya (cc'd) will draft the CAIQ mapping and Ben will coordinate the evidence delivery. If helpful, let's book 30 minutes tomorrow to walk through the playbook.

-Rachel
Rachel Kim
Customer Security Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morris <elena.morris@medicorp.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: LegalOps <legalops@medicorp.com>, andre.pierce@medicorp.com
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data lifecycle clarifications and CAIQ mapping request

Rachel — thanks for the quick turnaround. Couple of follow-ups after reading the summary: 

- Confirm that during the archival period archived objects remain searchable by your internal tooling and therefore subject to SAR discovery. If they are searchable, we need a documented access control and approval trail for any retrievals.

- For the irreversible purge: does Redwood perform a cryptographic shred (e.g., delete KEK/rotate KMS keys tied to archived objects) or rely solely on object deletion from storage lifecycle? Our legal team will accept either, but needs explicit description and evidence of the technique used.

- Evidence format: for the sample proof-of-delete package please include: (1) object list before purge, (2) lifecycle job's log entries (with timestamps and job IDs), (3) storage provider's delete confirmations, and (4) the retention policy revision history showing the policy that authorized the purge.

Also, please flag any SIG/CAIQ questions that you can't map to an existing artifact (we'll compile them into our gap list).

If you can get Priya's mapping by EOD Tue we can decide whether Legal needs to raise an exception.

Best,
Elena

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@medicorp.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 16:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data lifecycle clarifications and CAIQ mapping request

Elena — quick status update and answers inline (copying Priya and Markus for technical detail).

1) Searchability during archival: archived objects remain discoverable by our internal retrieval tooling but only via an audited workflow (ticket + approver). Retrievals are logged (audit entry includes requester, approver, object IDs, timestamps). We'll include a sample ticket and the corresponding access log extract in the evidence package.

2) Purge mechanism: Redwood implements object deletion plus key-rotation-backed irrecoverability for certain archival classes. For standard archival buckets the lifecycle job issues deletes to the object store and we capture the provider's delete confirmations. For the "cryptoshred" class (used when customers request stronger irreversibility), we rotate/destroy the envelope key in our KMS and record the KMS operation ID in the purge logs. We'll include both types of artifact examples.

3) Evidence contents & delivery: Priya's CAIQ/SIG mapping (attached) maps each requested question to an artifact. We'll deliver: 
   - object_manifest_prepurge.csv (synthetic)
   - lifecycle_job_20260922.log (job run output)
   - storage_delete_confirmations.pdf (provider responses)
   - retention_policy_history.json (audit-friendly format)
   - sample_access_ticket.pdf (redacted)

We've attached the archival playbook and a short checklist for the evidence package (redwood_archival-sunset-playbook.pdf). Expect the full artifact bundle in 4 business days; if Medicorp wants the cryptoshred artifacts for an actual tenant we will need Legal sign-off for the deletion window and a short exception form (we can provide the form).

Next steps:
- Priya: finalize CAIQ mapping and drop to the shared Drive link by EOD (action).
- Ben: coordinate SRE to run synthetic purge and package logs (action).
- Elena/Legal: confirm whether you require cryptoshred on production tenant or synthetic package is sufficient.

If you'd like a walkthrough of the artifacts, I'm happy to schedule 30 minutes on Friday.

Thanks — Rachel
Rachel Kim
Customer Security Manager | Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_archival-sunset-playbook.pdf (application/pdf)
